Accused person Judgment: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as Pfa Act), alleging that the accused have violated the provisions of t
texts.facts: he PFA Act and Rules. 2. As per the complaint, 28.04.2008 at about 8.00 PM, Food Inspector Ms. V.P.S. Chaudhary purchased a sample of "Paneer" for analysis from accused No. 1 Joginder Singh, M/s Moti Mahal Delux(a unit of south Asian) Hospitality Service Pvt. Ltd Plot No.10, V38 Mall, Laxmi Nagar, Delhi 110092 where the said food article was found stored for use in preparation of vegetable and whereas accused no. 1 Joginder Singh was found vending the article of food at the time of taking the sample. The sample consisted of 750 gm. of Paneer (ready for use) taken from open tray bearing no label declaration. The sample of "Paneer" was taken under the supervision/direction of Sh. Radha Charan, SDM/LHA. The sample was taken after proper mixing after cutting in to smallest possible pieces with the help of clean and dry knife in a clean and dry tray. Food inspector divided the sample of the article of food into three equal parts then and there by putting them into three clean and dry glass bottles. 20 drops of formalin was added in each counter part with the help of clean and dry DA vs Joginder Singh & Ors dropper. Each bottle containing the sample was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to the PFA Act, 1954 & Rules,1955. The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and wrapper of the bottles containing the sample. Notice in Form VI was prepared and the label of poly packets was reproduced on it and the copy of the same was given the vendor accused No. 1 Joginder Singh and the price of sample was also offered to him vide vendor receipt dated 28.04.2008. Panchnama too was prepared at the spot. All the documents prepared by the Food Inspector were signed by accused No.1 Joginder Singh by the other witness Sh.Jagdish Prasad, F.A. Before taking the sample efforts were made to get the public witnesses to join the proceedings but none came forward, as such Sh. Jagdish Prasad, PA was joined as witness. 3. One counter-part of the sample bearing LHA Code Number 22/LHA/22127 in intact condition along with copy of memo in Form VII and another copy of memo in Form Vll under seal cover were sent to separately to Public Analyst, Delhi on 29.04.08 and two counterparts of the sample along with two copies of memo in Form Vll were deposited with the SDM/LHA in intact conditions. All copies of memos in Form Vll bear the seal impression with which sample were sealed. Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the sample not conforming to standard. The report of Public Analyst is as follows:- "The sample does not conform to standard because milk fat of dried matter is less than prescribed minimum limit of 50%. 4. It is the case of the complainant that accused No. 1 Joginder DA vs Joginder Singh & Ors Singh was the vendor-cum-manager of M/s Moti Mahal Delux (a Unit of South Asian Hospitality Services Pvt. Ltd.), Plot No.10, V38 Mall, Laxmi Nagar, Delhi-110092 at the time of taking sample and as such he is incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of said unit of the Da vs Joginder Singh & Ors on 23 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174106905/ 2 company. M/s South Asian Hospitality Services Pvt. Ltd. is a company having three directors i.e. Ms. Bela Juneja, Ms Kiran Juneja and accused No. 3 Himan Juneja. Accused No. 3 Himan Juneja is the only working Director and looks after the day to day business of the company and as such he is incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the said unit of the company. Being a company M/s South Asian Hospitality Services Pvt. Ltd. is also liable. M/s South Asian Hospitality Services Pvt. Ltd. is having its corporate office at 30 Power House, Building, 4'" Floor. Hauz Khas Village, New Delhi-110 016 and its registered office at 40/43, llnd Floor, Chittranjan Park, New Delhi-110019. The vendor and the Managing-cum-Whole Time Director of the company did not disclose to the food inspector the name, address and other particulars of the person from whom they had purchased the sampled article of food "Paneer". 5. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 16.07.2010 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(a)&(m) of the PFA Act 1954 as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act against the accused wherein the cognizance of the complaint was not taken bearing barred by limitation. Thereafter, the complainant approached learned Session Court and vide order dated 08.11.2010, learned DA vs Joginder Singh & Ors Sessions Court [LEAKAGE_MASK] the order dated 16.07.2010. 6. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned initially and later on other accused were also summoned. The accused no.1 thereafter exercised his option of analysing the counter part through CFL under section 13 (2) of the PFA Act. Based on the report of the CFL notice was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1) (a) and (C) PFA Act being violation of Section 2(ia)(a)&(m) of PFA Act, to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 7. At the trial, the prosecution examined five witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 FI Sh. V.P.S. Chaudhary, PW-2 SDM/LHA Ms. Radha Charan, PW-4 SDM/LHA Sh Hukam Singh, PW-5 FA Sh Jagdish Prasad. PW-1 and PW-5 were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh. Radha Charan. These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample commodity of "Paneer" 750 gms from the vendor for analysis, bearing no label or declaration, taking the sample of Paneer after cutting into smallest possible pieces with the help of a clean & dry knife in a clean and dry tray, dividing the sample into three equal parts by putting them into three separate clean and dry sample bottles, putting 20 drops of formalin in each sample bottle with the help of dry & clean dropper, separately sealing, packing and marking the same and DA vs Joginder Singh & Ors obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex.PW- 1/A, Notice in form VI Ex. PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C. Thereafter, on the next working day i.e. 29.04.2008 one counterpart alongwith a copy of Memo in Form VII in a sealed packet and another copy of Memo in Form VII in a separate sealed cover were deposited with PA vide PA's Receipt Ex.PW1/D and the remaining two counterparts alongwith two copies of Memo in Form VII in a sealed packet were deposited with LHA on 29.04.2008 vide LHA Receipt Ex. PW 1/E under intimation that one counterpart of the sample has already been deposited with the PA. PW 1/F was received through LHA stating that the sample was not conforming to the standards. On the directions of SDM /LHA, PW-1 FI V.P.S. Chaudhary started the investigations and during investigation, he sent a letter Ex. PW1/G to STO Ward no. 88 for seeking information on the constitution of M/s Moti Mahel Delux (a unit of South Asian Hospitality Service Pvt. Ltd), Plot no. 10, V3S Mall, Laxmi Nagar, Delhi and received its reply stating that one Sh. Parveen Juneja was Director-cum Authorized signatory of the same. He also sent a letter to Moti Mahel Delux and two letters to South Asian Hospitality Service Pvt. Ltd at their various addresses vide Ex. PW1/H, Ex. PW1/H1 and Ex. PW1H2 and received its reply vide Ex.PW1/H3 and document Ex.P1. Thereafter, PW-1 put the entire case file before the concerned SDM / LHA, who forwarded the same to the then Director PFA for obtaining his Consent and the then Director PFA Shri K.R. Kishore granted his Consent Ex. PW 1/I for prosecution of accused persons after applying his mind. During the tiral PW-3 FI Hukam Singh prepared the DA vs Joginder Singh & Ors application Ex.PW4/A for condonation of Delhi and thereafter the present complaint Ex.PW4/B was filed before the Court. These witnesses were duly cross-examined by Ld. Defence Counsel. 8. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC were recorded on 21.07.2018 wherein the accused denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. The accused chooses not to lead defence evidence accordingly the matter was fixed for final arguments.
texts.arguments: 12. In Calcutta Municipal Corporation v. Pawan Kumar Saraf [AIR 1999 SC 738], it has been authoritatively laid down that the legal impact of a certificate of the Director of CFL is three fold: (a) it DA vs Joginder Singh & Ors annuls or replaces the report of the PA, (b) it gains finality regarding the quality and standard of the food article involved in the case and (c) it becomes irrefutable so far as the facts stated therein are concerned. 13. In Subhash Chander v. State, Delhi Administration [1983(4) DRJ 100], it was observed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi that "It has repeatedly been held by the supreme court that the certificate of the Director supersedes the report of the public analyst and is to be treated as conclusive evidence of its contents. In the landmark judgement titled as MCD v. Bishan Sarup [ILR 1970 (1) Delhi 518], the full bench of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi observed as under:- (a)The accused is entitled to get benefit of doubt if on account of delay or lapse on the part of prosecution to institute a prosecution, the Director CFL is unable to analyse the sample because of delay DA vs Joginder Singh & Ors or of the sample undergoes a change for this reason. ( b)Once On this basis, the defence is seeking to claim that the samples were not representative due to said 'variations of more than 0.3%' in PA and CFL report. 16. In this regard, the defence strongly relies upon the judgement titled as Kanshi Nath v. State [2005(2) FAC 219], informing that the said ruling has been constantly followed by the Hon'ble High DA vs Joginder Singh & Ors Court of Delhi in many other decisions. 17. This issue of variation was considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Delhi Administration vs Vidya Gupta Criminal Appeal No. 625 of 2018 dated 24.04.2018 wherein it was held that the finding of Hon'ble High Court in Kanshi Nath vs State and State vs Mahender Kumar & Ors, which hold that if in the comparison of reports of PA and the Director vast variations are found, then the samples are not representative, is improper. Those decisions do not lay down good law.
